chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and Sindi ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn al-Walid, all from Asim ibn Humayd, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, who said:
I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from the Qummis asked him, saying: 'O Abu Abdillah, do women pray over the dead bodies?'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) shed the blood of al-Mughira ibn Abi al-'As.' And he narrated a long hadith: 'And indeed, Zaynab, the daughter of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), passed away, and indeed Fatimah (peace be upon her) went out with her women and prayed over her sister.'
ai.seo_question: Do women pray over the dead bodies in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the permissibility of women performing the funeral prayer by citing the precedent of Fatimah (peace be upon her) leading the prayer for her sister Zaynab. This hadith is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it establishes the practice based on the actions of the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the validity of women's participation in communal rituals beyond mere attendance.
